Since the guard change is intentional and now documented in the WP spec, it would be worth updating the inline comment on that PATCH block to reference the regex rather than startsWith for future maintainers.

theme-init.js uses var which is appropriate for ES5 (per the WP constraint), but a JSDoc comment at the top explaining that ES5 is intentional (to avoid needing a separate build step for this one file) would help future contributors avoid 'upgrading' it to let/const inadvertently.

comments.note: No Critical or High findings — all OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed across all 4 modified files. Full audit scope: A01 (Broken Access Control) — slug validation via PROJECT_SLUG_REGEX in _validateSlug() prevents path traversal into the .knowledge/ directory; scope-based store selection correctly restricts operations to the targeted store. A02 (Cryptographic Failures) — no cryptographic changes introduced; CSP tightening (script-src 'self') is a net positive. A03 (Injection) — tags values from the comma-split query string are used only for in-memory array membership tests (insight.tags.includes(tag)); query string reaches only .toLowerCase().includes() on in-memory data; no SQL, shell, template, or DOM-sink injection surface. A04 (Insecure Design) — tag filter ordering (text match → tag intersection → offset/limit slice) is correct and mirrors the listInsights() pattern exactly. A05 (Security Misconfiguration) — removal of unsafe-inline from script-src is a direct CSP improvement; theme-init.js IIFE uses no eval or dangerous APIs. A06 (Vulnerable Components) — no new third-party dependencies added. A07 (Auth/Session) — no changes to authentication or session flows. A08 (Data Integrity) — no deserialization changes; Zod schema validation (.strict()) on all write paths unchanged. A09 (Security Logging) — error paths continue to write to process.stderr; no security-event audit gaps introduced. A10 (SSRF) — no server-side URL fetching added.

[Low / Defence-in-depth] mcp-server/gui/api-knowledge.ts — handleListKnowledge(): the tags query parameter is split on commas and each segment trimmed/filtered, but there is no explicit upper-bound on the number of tag values accepted. A caller could supply a very long comma-separated list (e.g. 10 000 tags) causing O(n*m) tag-intersection work in searchInsights(). Given this is a localhost-only internal dashboard the practical risk is negligible, but capping tags at a reasonable limit (e.g. 50) would be a defence-in-depth improvement for future exposure.
